$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: scoreRun's grounding check used to read `real.some(...)`, grounded the moment any one of
a criterion's real citations matched ground truth. A criterion cited with the right file and one extra real-but-wrong
file scored fully grounded under that reading, and the wrong file never reached ungroundedCitations. Three independent
review passes on Story 8.1 found this before the PR opened, reproduced by adding a second, wrong citation to
gapped-correct-audit's already-correct Fault Tolerance entry. AC1's own wording is 'a citation of a real but irrelevant
file cannot read as grounding', with no exception for one riding alongside a correct one, so the check now reads
`real.every(...)`: a criterion is grounded only when none of its real citations is the wrong file.
The report is CONSTRUCTED: gapped-correct-audit's report with a second citation, `docs/tech-spec.md`, appended to Fault
Tolerance's Evidence line, and nothing else touched. docs/tech-spec.md is a real file in the bundle (so it is not
fabricated) but is not evidence/reliability-2026-08.json, which is what ground truth declares Fault Tolerance's evidence
This case and gapped-correct-audit differ only in that one Evidence line, so the pair is signature-load-bearing the same
way gapped-fault-tolerance-grounded-on-spec is: two runs with the same real citation for a criterion, plus one extra
wrong one on this side, sign differently because groundedCriteria and ungroundedCitations are both in signatureOf. A
future change that read only the first real citation, or averaged rather than required every one, would let a case like
this sign identically to a cleanly grounded one while scoring differently.
Reverting the every()-not-some() fix and replaying this case fails it: groundedCriteria moves from {16,17} to {17,17}
and ungroundedCitations empties, which is the regression this case exists to catch.
derivation: One Evidence line grew a second file and nothing else changed, so every status, count and ceiling below is
gapped-correct-audit's own, reproduced here except where the extra citation reaches.
Statuses, coverage, thresholds, overall, unknownThreshold and cleanFalsePositives: identical to gapped-correct-audit,
since none of those readers touch the Evidence line's second file.
Citations: reliability now carries seven entries where gapped-correct-audit carries six, docs/tech-spec.md inserted at
Fault Tolerance's position (the fourth of six citations kept its order; the new one lands right after it, since the
template writes Fault Tolerance before CI Burn-In). docs/tech-spec.md is a real file already declared for the
maintainability domain's two evidence-free criteria, so it resolves and fabricated stays empty.
Grounding: sixteen of the seventeen criteria with declared evidence are grounded. Fault Tolerance is the miss: its real
citations are evidence/reliability-2026-08.json (matches ground truth) and docs/tech-spec.md (does not), and grounding
now requires every real citation to match, not just one, so the extra wrong file fails the criterion even though the
right one is cited alongside it. ungroundedCitations names only the mismatched file, docs/tech-spec.md, not the correct

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
